level.title: Korean A1+ — A day and a call
goals: Tell the time and describe a day hour by hour
Answer the phone, take a message and text back
Invite somebody, accept, and decline without giving offence

lessons.title: 몇 시에 일어나요?
lessons.learn: A daily routine is a list of verbs on a clock: 일어나요, 씻어요, 먹어요, 가요. The hour takes the Sino-Korean numbers and the particle 에, and it normally comes before the verb.

grammar.title: Telling the hour
grammar.pattern: 일곱 시에 일어나요 · 아홉 시에 출근해요 · 몇 시에 자요?
grammar.explain: Hours use the Sino-Korean numbers with the counter 시: 한 시, 두 시, 일곱 시. A clock time takes 에 and stands before the verb; 아침, 점심 and 저녁 do not take 에 at all.

examples.en: I get up at seven in the morning.
I go to work at nine.
I usually go to bed at eleven.

mistakes.why: The hour comes before the verb, not after it.
One 에 is enough; 아침, 점심 and 저녁 take it once.

dialogue.en: What time do you usually get up?

dialogue.t: 일곱 시에 일어나요. 그리고 아홉 시에 출근해요.
dialogue.r: ilgop si-e ireonayo. geurigo ahop si-e chulgeunhaeyo.
dialogue.en: At seven. And I go to work at nine.
Where do you have lunch?

dialogue.t: 회사 근처에서 먹어요. 보통 김밥을 먹어요.
dialogue.r: hoesa geuncheo-eseo meogeoyo. botong gimbab-eul meogeoyo.
dialogue.en: Near the office. Usually gimbap.

lessons.title: 주말에는 뭐 해요?
lessons.learn: Frequency words sit in front of the verb and shape the whole answer: 항상, 보통, 자주, 가끔, 거의 안. The contrast between weekday and weekend is marked with 는.

grammar.title: How often
grammar.pattern: 주말에는 자주 운동해요 · 가끔 영화를 봐요 · 거의 안 나가요
grammar.explain: Frequency adverbs are placed immediately before the verb, and 거의 needs a negative after it. The particle 는 on 주말에는 contrasts the weekend with the rest of the week.

examples.en: At the weekend I often exercise.
Sometimes I watch a film.
These days I hardly go out.

mistakes.why: The time phrase opens the sentence it belongs to.
가끔 is positive; a negative sentence takes 거의 안 or 별로.

dialogue.en: What do you usually do at the weekend?
On Saturday I do the laundry and clean.
Do you work on Sunday too?

dialogue.t: 아니요, 일요일에는 거의 안 나가고 집에서 쉬어요.
dialogue.r: aniyo, iryoil-e-neun geoui an nagago jib-eseo swieoyo.
dialogue.en: No, on Sunday I hardly go out and rest at home.

lessons.title: 몇 시까지 해요?
lessons.learn: Opening hours are asked with 몇 시부터 몇 시까지. 부터 marks the start, 까지 the end, and both can stand alone: 아홉 시부터, 여섯 시까지.

grammar.title: From and until
grammar.pattern: 몇 시부터 몇 시까지 해요? · 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지 · 일요일에는 쉬어요
grammar.explain: 부터 and 까지 can be used as a pair or separately, and they attach directly to the time. A closed day is stated with a plain negative sentence, not with 까지.

examples.en: From what time until what time are you open?
We are open from nine until six.
We close on Sundays.

mistakes.why: 부터 marks the start on its own; it does not follow 까지.
까지 is a stretch of time; a recurring closed day takes 에는.

dialogue.t: 이 가게는 몇 시부터 몇 시까지 해요?
dialogue.r: i gage-neun myeot si-buteo myeot si-kkaji haeyo?
dialogue.en: From when until when is this shop open?
From nine until six.
Are you open at the weekend too?
We open on Saturday and close on Sunday.

lessons.title: 여보세요?
lessons.learn: A phone call opens with 여보세요, which is used only on the phone. The caller identifies itself, and 잠깐만요 buys a moment.

grammar.title: On the phone
grammar.pattern: 여보세요? · 지훈 씨 계세요? · 잠깐만요 · 바꿔 드릴게요
grammar.explain: 여보세요 belongs to the phone and to nothing else. To ask for a person use 계세요, and to pass the phone on use the humble 바꿔 드리다.

examples.en: Hello, is Jihun there?
One moment. I will pass you over.
He is on the phone right now.

mistakes.why: On the phone 여보세요 does the greeting; the errand follows immediately.
받다 is already the whole verb of answering.

dialogue.en: Hello?
Hello, this is Jihun. Is Mina there?
Yes, one moment. I will pass you over.
Thank you.

lessons.title: 문자를 보내요
lessons.learn: Texting has its own short verbs: 보내다, 받다, 답장을 하다, 읽다. A message that arrives late is answered with 늦게 답장해서 미안합니다.

grammar.title: Sending and replying
grammar.pattern: 문자를 보냈어요 · 답장이 없었어요 · 늦게 답장해서 미안해요
grammar.explain: The message is the object of 보내다 and 답장 is the object of 하다. A reason with -아서/어서 joins the lateness to the apology, and 나중에 stands before the verb it modifies.

examples.en: I sent a text.
There is no reply yet.
I will reply later.

mistakes.why: 답장 takes one verb: 보내다 or 하다, not both.
One ending per sentence.

dialogue.en: Did you send the text yesterday?
Yes, I sent it, but there was no reply.
Sorry, I read it late.
It is fine. Reply when you can.

lessons.title: 메시지를 남겨요
lessons.learn: When the person is out the call becomes a message: 다시 전화해 달라고 전해 주세요. The promise to call back takes -(으)ㄹ게요.

vocab.en: a call, talking on the phone

grammar.title: Leaving a message
grammar.pattern: 메시지를 남길게요 · 다시 전화해 달라고 전해 주세요 · 나중에 다시 걸게요
grammar.explain: A request passed on to a third person takes -아/어 달라고 하다. The promise to do something for the listener takes -(으)ㄹ게요, which is softer than -(으)ㄹ 거예요.

examples.en: I will leave a message.
Please tell him to call back.
I will ring again later.

mistakes.why: A request made on someone else's behalf takes -달라고, not -주세요.
One verb per sentence: 남기다 already means leave it.

dialogue.en: Hello, is Mina there?
She is not at her desk. Would you like to leave a message?

dialogue.t: 네, 다시 전화해 달라고 전해 주세요.
dialogue.r: ne, dasi jeonhwahae dallago jeonhae juseyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, please tell her to call back.
Understood. I will pass that on.

lessons.title: 우리 집에 놀러 오세요
lessons.learn: An invitation is 놀러 오세요 or 같이 …ㄹ까요? and the answer names the day. A visit brings something small: 과일이나 케이크면 충분해요.

grammar.title: Inviting
grammar.pattern: 우리 집에 놀러 오세요 · 토요일 어때요? · 뭘 가져갈까요?
grammar.explain: The invitation is a request form with a soft ending, and the reply can propose a day. Asking what to bring takes the plain -(으)ㄹ까요? with a neutral object.

examples.en: Come over to my place.
How about Saturday afternoon?
What shall I bring?

mistakes.why: 놀러 comes directly before 오다.
One verb: 사다 buys it, 가져가다 brings it.

dialogue.t: 이번 주말에 우리 집에 놀러 오세요.
dialogue.r: ibeon jumal-e uri jib-e nolleo oseyo.
dialogue.en: Come over to my place this weekend.
Great. How about Saturday afternoon?
Fine. What shall I bring?
Nothing is needed. Fruit is plenty.

lessons.title: 미안하지만 못 가요
lessons.learn: A refusal keeps the relationship: 미안하지만, 그날은 어려워요, 다음에 꼭 갈게요. The hard part is said first and the alternative last.

grammar.title: Declining politely
grammar.pattern: 미안하지만 그날은 어려워요 · 사정이 있어서 못 가요 · 다음에 꼭 갈게요
grammar.explain: The refusal opens with 미안하지만 or 죄송하지만 and states the difficulty without a reason; the reason, if given at all, is brief. The promise for next time closes the message and takes 꼭.

examples.en: I am sorry, but that day is difficult.
Something has come up that day, so I cannot come.
I will certainly come next time.

mistakes.why: One clause, one ending — the apology and the refusal are not two sentences bolted together.
A promise to the host takes -(으)ㄹ게요, which offers it; -(으)ㄹ 거예요 only predicts.

lessons.title: 방문 예절
lessons.learn: A Korean home is entered with the shoes off and a greeting at the door: 들어가면서 인사해요. Gifts pass from both hands, and the host's offering is received rather than refused outright.

grammar.title: When you visit
grammar.pattern: 신발을 벗고 들어가요 · 두 손으로 드려요 · 앉으라고 하세요
grammar.explain: Sequence is made with -고: 신발을 벗고 들어가요, take off your shoes and go in. Giving something to an elder uses the humble 드리다 and both hands, never one.

examples.en: You take off your shoes and go in.
A gift is given with both hands.
Please sit. I will bring tea.

mistakes.why: An elder receives something with 드리다, and 께 marks them.
Two actions in sequence are joined by -고.

dialogue.en: Welcome. Leave your shoes here.
Yes, hello. I gave your mother the gift.
Thank you. Please sit. I will bring tea.
Thank you. The house feels really warm.

items.q: 신발을 벗고 들어가고 선물은 두 손으로 드려요. What is this about?
내일 일곱 시에 만나요. When are they meeting?

culture.text: Korea runs on messaging. 카카오톡 is on nearly every phone, and a reply that takes a day is read as a statement in itself — 빠른 답장 is a social expectation rather than a courtesy. A phone call opens with 여보세요 and identifies the caller immediately, because the number alone rarely says who is speaking. Invitations are informal and flexible: 놀러 오세요 can be issued and accepted within one exchange of texts, and the refusal carries its own grammar of apology and promise for next time.

reading.text: 어제 저녁에 친구에게서 전화가 왔습니다. 저는 여보세요 하고 받았습니다. 친구가 이번 주말에 자기 집에 놀러 오라고 했습니다. 저는 토요일 오후에 가겠다고 했습니다. 오늘 아침에 다시 문자가 왔습니다. 무엇을 가져오면 좋겠냐고 물었습니다. 제가 과일을 사겠다고 답장했습니다. 친구는 아무것도 필요 없다고 했지만 저는 가는 길에 과일을 살 것입니다.
reading.gloss: Yesterday evening a friend called me. I answered with hello. My friend asked me to come over to their place this weekend. I said I would go on Saturday afternoon. This morning a text came again. They asked what would be good to bring. I replied that I would buy fruit. My friend said nothing is needed, but I will buy fruit on the way.

listening.script:
미나: 여보세요?
지훈: 안녕하세요, 지훈입니다. 미나 씨 계세요?
미나: 네, 저예요. 무슨 일이세요?
지훈: 오늘 저녁에 시간 있어요? 같이 밥을 먹을까요?
미나: 오늘은 어려워요. 내일은 어때요?
지훈: 좋아요. 내일 일곱 시에 만나요.
listening.gloss: Mina: Hello? Jihun: Hello, this is Jihun. Is Mina there? Mina: Yes, speaking. What is it? Jihun: Do you have time this evening? Shall we eat together? Mina: Today is difficult. How about tomorrow? Jihun: Good. Let us meet at seven tomorrow.

mistakes.why: On the phone 여보세요 replaces the greeting; the errand comes next.
A request passed on for somebody else takes -달라고, not -주세요.
Polish the refusal with one ending: 미안하지만 plus 어려워요.

task.title: Write a day and a message
task.instructions: Write your weekday in six sentences with times, then write a phone call of four turns: greeting, errand, hold, message. Use 여보세요 once, -(으)ㄹ게요 twice and one refusal with 미안하지만.
